page: Microsoft Azure NV6s_v2 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 6 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs and an allocation of 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding 18.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA M60 GPU equipped with 8 GB of video memory. In addition, the instance includes 790 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations.

The hardware configuration pairs moderate host compute with high system memory density and discrete graphics processing. With over 18 GB of host RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive datasets can be staged locally without exhausting system resources. The integrated 790 GB solid-state drive offers local high-speed scratch space for intermediate file handling and visual caching. A key hardware tradeoff is the legacy NVIDIA M60 architecture, which lacks modern tensor-acceleration features found in newer generation accelerators, limiting its efficiency for large-scale machine learning training compared to workstation visual tasks.

Qualitatively, the NV6s_v2 balances resource allocation for applications that require dedicated graphical processing without the overhead of enterprise deep-learning accelerator classes. This profile aligns directly with workloads such as virtual desktop infrastructure, computer-aided design, 3D modeling, remote workstation streaming, and video transcoding.
description: Microsoft Azure NV6s_v2 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for graphics-focused and memory-demanding technical workloads. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 6 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs paired with 112.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 18.67 GB per core. Graphic processing and compute acceleration are delivered via a single NVIDIA M60 GPU featuring 8 GB of dedicated video RAM. Local storage consists of 790 GB of high-speed solid-state drive capacity, supplemented by Premium Storage capability. The combination of dedicated vCPUs, generous host memory, and integrated GPU acceleration makes this instance effective for virtual desktop infrastructure, 3D visualization, computer-aided design, video encoding, and graphics rendering, while the older generation accelerator represents a tradeoff for deep learning workloads that require modern tensor hardware.
